### 1. The Court’s Holding

In *Cooper v. Feeney*, 2023 OH 3164, the Ohio Supreme Court held:

> “When the market value of lost or destroyed personal property is essentially indeterminable, the proper measure of damages is the *standard value* of the property to the owner.  The standard value is determined by considering, in order of priority: (1) the original cost of the property; (2) the replacement cost; (3) the salvage value; and (4) the fair market value at the time of loss.  The plaintiff must prove ownership by documentary evidence such as receipts, invoices, or photographs.” (para. 12)
